title: Aaron Bell's mother and cutting Aaron's hair
summary: He explains how Aaron Bell's well-trained mother played in his church and taught his sister, and recalls cutting young Aaron's hair in barbering class.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: : Well, there's one thing. Where did Aaron Bell's mother come in the picture?
Aaron Bell's mother. That's what I was intending to get to when we first started talking. And that was -- now, you know, when I used to go to church?
: Yeah.
She used to play for the church choir.
: Yeah.
And oh, I used to get the biggest kick out of listening to her play. I enjoyed her playing. And you know, it's things like them that I think that have to wake me up about music.
: She was well-trained.

She was well-trained and could sing and his dad played trombone and his dad would play the trombone in the church along with her and the choir and then she also taught my sister piano lessons, see? And she was the one I really wanted to take lessons from, but the folks, you know, -- because I enjoyed her playing, you know.
: But you never did get lessons from her?
Never did get a chance to get lessons from her. But my sister did, see.
Yeah.

And that family -- that was some musical family, you know. He had -- Aaron had brothers and sisters -- he had a sister who played real good, real great. I don't know what she's doing now, what she did later. But I mean, she was there musically. Had a couple other brothers who was there musically.
Did you know him there?
Aaron?
Yes.

Yes. I used to cut Aaron's hair in school. You know, I was about 11th or 12th grade, see, when they'd send the younger kids over there to get their haircuts when we took barbering in school and Aaron would -- I'd always get him and I'd cut his hair and he'd just be tickling, laughing, "Hee, hee," and I never could give him a good haircut because he would laugh all the time I was cutting his hair.
(Laughter.)
We were talking about that at Michael's this past summer and he remembers it. That was so funny. Yes. But Aaron, he --
Well, Aaron was younger than you then.
Yes, yes. He was younger. See, now,
he was in grade school, see, when I was about my 11th grade, see. That's how they'd send the grade schools over for us to cut their hair.
Oh, I got you.
Yes.
